clue.text: Clearly excited with archer's first arrow case

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word it follows, the archer's

blocks.note: the opening letter of archer
a quiver is the case an archer carries arrows in

explanation.surface: An archer, thrilled, reaches for the first arrow in the case.
explanation.walkthrough: The archery picture makes the quiver feel like scenery, but it is the bulk of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone visibly trembling with eagerness is aquiver, an adjective for obvious agitation or excitement.

clue.text: Film slyest lover regularly viewed as an excuse for a kiss?

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every other one, from the two words before it

blocks.note: a film of moisture or haze is a mist
second, fourth and sixth letters of slyest
second and fourth letters of lover

explanation.surface: A sly film lover pretends to see something as an excuse to steal a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: by Christmas custom, anyone standing under the hanging sprig may be kissed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christmas custom of kissing beneath a hung sprig makes the plant a festive pretext for a kiss.

clue.text: Used to be a means of writing by hand, ignoring the onset of copy and paste

indicators.note: ignoring tells us to leave out the named letter from the pen's name
'the onset of' keeps only the first letter of 'copy'

blocks.note: past tense of to be
taken as written
Bic is the brand of ballpoint pen
first letter of copy, to be removed

explanation.surface: Handwriting has given way to copy and paste on the computer.
explanation.walkthrough: Copy and paste reads as the computing phrase; in fact paste alone is the definition. Drop the C from BIC to leave BI.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasabi is the hot green Japanese horseradish condiment, usually served as a paste with sushi.

clue.text: All others fall: hold back!

blocks.note: the rest means all the others
rain is a fall of water from the sky

explanation.surface: A command to stop everyone else from falling: hold back!
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to check or keep under control, which is exactly holding something back.

clue.text: Agents of a vet's enterprise at sixes and sevens

indicators.note: at sixes and sevens means in disarray, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: all fifteen letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: A veterinary practice's agents are in total confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Representatives act on behalf of someone else, which is what agents do.

clue.text: Atomizer: special science fiction weapon

blocks.note: sp is a dictionary abbreviation for special
the ray gun is the classic weapon of science fiction

explanation.surface: A sci-fi device that turns out to be a special weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Most solvers would expect S for special; here the less common abbreviation SP is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomizer turns liquid into a fine mist, which is what a spray gun does with paint.

clue.text: Female ruff borne on the wings of finches in shoals

indicators.note: wings are the two sides, so only the outermost letters of the following word are kept

blocks.note: a ree (or reeve) is the female of the ruff, a wading bird
first and last letters of finches

explanation.surface: A bird carried along among flocks of finches.
explanation.walkthrough: The ruff here is a wading bird, not a collar; its female is called a ree or reeve, a word that turns up mainly in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoal can mean a sandbank or shallow underwater ridge, the same hazard as a reef.

clue.text: One church composer who shows no emotion?

definitions.note: elliptical: one who shows no emotion, the One doing double duty in the surface

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
CE is the Church of England
Alban Berg, the Austrian composer

explanation.surface: A church composer who remains utterly unmoved.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a figurative definition: a cold, unfeeling person is called an iceberg.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone an iceberg is a figure of speech for a person who is cold and emotionally reserved.

clue.text: One bird American put back in golden eagle genus

indicators.note: put back means taking a letter out of its place and moving it to the end of the word

blocks.note: a, as in one of something
a quail is a small game bird
A is an abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An American bird is reclassified into the genus of the golden eagle.
explanation.walkthrough: The A inside QUAIL is taken as the American and moved to the back of the bird, giving QUILA after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquila is the scientific genus name of the golden eagle and its close relatives, from Latin for eagle.

clue.text: Negotiated cut around line

indicators.note: around says the first word's letters go on either side of the next one

blocks.note: pared means trimmed or cut
a ley is a line, as in ley line

explanation.surface: A deal was struck by cutting round a line.
explanation.walkthrough: A ley line is the supposed alignment of ancient sites; ley alone serves crosswords as line.
explanation.definitionFit: To parley is to hold talks with an opponent, so parleyed is a past-tense synonym for negotiated.

clue.text: Going between flyers providing publicity ahead of a trio playing

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of the phrase before it are being played about with
ahead of fixes the order, putting the first piece in front of the second

blocks.note: to give something an airing is to publicise it
fodder, five letters

explanation.surface: Pilots get publicity before a trio of musicians performs.
explanation.walkthrough: Ahead of tells us AIR comes before the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Air-to-air describes weapons or communication passing from one aircraft to another in flight.

clue.text: They agree part unfortunately missing from arranged repayments

indicators.note: missing from says those letters are absent from the word that follows
arranged means put into a new order, so the remaining letters are reordered

blocks.note: the four letters of part, unfortunately suggesting they are scattered through the longer word
taken as written before letters are removed

explanation.surface: Creditors agree to rearranged repayments, with one portion sadly missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing P, A, R and T from REPAYMENTS leaves E, Y, M, E, N, S to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men are sycophants who always concur with their superiors, so they are people who agree.

clue.text: Dissidents present idiosyncratic behavioural features

blocks.note: here means present, as in a register
tics are habitual quirks or twitches

explanation.surface: Rebels display odd personal quirks.
explanation.walkthrough: Present is the adjective, as in answering a roll call, not a gift or a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Heretics hold opinions contrary to established doctrine, which makes them dissenters or dissidents.

clue.text: Old material of base gibe, a hollow gaucherie

indicators.note: hollow means emptied of its inside, so only the outer letters of the word remain

blocks.note: e is the base of natural logarithms
a quip is a witty remark or gibe
taken as written
first and last letters of gaucherie

explanation.surface: An old cloth carries a crude, empty taunt and some clumsiness.
explanation.walkthrough: Base as e comes from mathematics, the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipage is an archaic word for equipment or outfit, the gear and material needed for an undertaking.

clue.text: Way of carrying greedy football player?

blocks.note: piggy as an adjective means greedy
a back is a defensive player in football

explanation.surface: A gluttonous footballer gets carried off.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the surface is a fanciful picture of a greedy defender.
explanation.definitionFit: A piggyback is a ride on someone's back and shoulders, a familiar method of carrying a person.

clue.text: Mini avalanche of Coke and lager knocked over

indicators.note: knocked over in a down entry turns the word upside down, so it is read backwards

blocks.note: snow is slang for cocaine, coke
Pils is pilsner lager

explanation.surface: A spilled cola and beer cause a small mess on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: Coke looks like the soft drink, but it is the drug, and snow is its slang name.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowslip is a small slide of snow down a slope, a minor form of avalanche.

clue.text: Brown loaf or cob?

blocks.note: hazel is a light brown colour
loaf and nut are both slang for the head

explanation.surface: At the bakery: a brown loaf, or a cob roll?
explanation.walkthrough: Loaf and cob both look like bread. Loaf is the head (as in use your loaf), and a cob is also a large hazelnut, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Cob is another name for the hazel tree and its large nuts, so a cob is one example of this nut.

clue.text: Like one-time partner, unable to occasionally go without it

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so just some letters, alternating, are taken

blocks.note: as means like
an ex is a former partner
first, third and fifth letters of unable

explanation.surface: Like a former partner who now and then cannot do without it.
explanation.walkthrough: It is a common crossword euphemism for sex, so being without it is having no sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Asexual means lacking sexual feeling or reproduction, so it is a coy way of saying lacking sex.

clue.text: Absolute head of newspaper getting used to Express

definitions.note: a past habit, so a past tense to match the answer

blocks.note: utter means absolute, complete
the editor, ED, heads a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper's editor is settling in at the Express.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on Express makes it look like the Daily Express newspaper; it is the plain verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to say aloud or voice, so uttered is the past tense of expressing something in words.

clue.text: Do away with a barrier involving sibling

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a plus gate, a barrier
bro is short for brother

explanation.surface: Remove a fence that is shutting in a brother.
explanation.walkthrough: Barrier is read with its article, a gate, and the sibling slips in between the two.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrogate a law or agreement is to repeal or abolish it, formally doing away with it.

clue.text: Maybe rat's lair amid decayed matter

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: rot is decay
a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: A rat makes its home among rotting rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for is, joining definition to wordplay, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats are gnawing mammals of the order Rodentia, so a rat is an example of this group.

clue.text: Make new sketch of Turn of the Screw

indicators.note: a turn of something here means turning it round, so the following word is read backwards

blocks.note: screw is British slang for a prison officer, a warder

explanation.surface: An artist re-does the illustrations for Henry James's ghost story The Turn of the Screw.
explanation.walkthrough: The novella title hides the device: Screw is prison slang for a warder.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraw something is to draw it again, which is making a fresh sketch of it.

clue.text: Marsupials must finally settle for the night

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: roos is short for kangaroos
the closing letter of must

explanation.surface: Kangaroos have to bed down at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds roost when they perch to sleep, so to roost is to settle down for the night.

clue.text: Obligated, certainly but empty inside

indicators.note: empty means the middle has been removed, keeping only the outer letters
inside tells us the reduced word is placed within the first word

blocks.note: indeed means certainly
first and last letters of but

explanation.surface: Bound by duty, certainly, but feeling hollow inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Empty applies to but, not to the surrounding word; that empty word then goes inside the word for certainly.
explanation.definitionFit: To be indebted is to owe something to someone, so it means being under an obligation.

clue.text: Former Balkan vessel returning, Victor too

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word it governs is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a jug is a vessel for liquid
also means too
V is Victor in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A former Balkan ship heads home, and a man called Victor as well.
explanation.walkthrough: Returning seems to attach to vessel, but it reverses too, which comes later in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Jugoslav is an older spelling of Yugoslav, a person from the former state of Yugoslavia.

clue.text: One who steals a pound

blocks.note: first meaning: a thief, from nick, slang for steal
second meaning: British slang for one pound sterling

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pickpocket lifting a single coin. In British slang a nicker is a pound, and to nick is to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick is British slang for steal, so a nicker is a thief; nicker is also slang for a pound sterling.

clue.text: Perhaps Tom hasn't succeeded in pursuit of dishy creature

indicators.note: hasn't means is without, so the named letter is dropped from the word
in pursuit of means following behind, so this piece comes after the next one

blocks.note: platy means flat like a plate, so dish-like
a tom is a male cat, an example of a puss
S is the abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A tom cat fails to catch an attractive animal it is chasing.
explanation.walkthrough: Dishy looks like attractive, but it is read as plate-like, PLATY. Remove S from PUSS to leave PUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The duck-billed platypus is an egg-laying Australian mammal, so it is an example of a creature.
